notes: Heading levels skip: jumps h1 to h5. Needs a person.
810 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 3 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Mailing Address" is an h5 with no h4 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 3 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — melissa.white@maine.gov → Melissa.White@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 30 links on this page open a file — 30 PDF — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: For media inquiries, contact Director of Communications Melissa White at Melissa.White@maine.gov.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Put the page’s one action in the banner
decisions.why: This page opens with a paragraph holding nothing but "Submit Questions, Comments, & Concerns Web Form" — the first thing it asks you to do, set as a line of body text. The banner has a place for exactly that, so it moves there as a button. The link and its words are unchanged; only where it sits changes.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (3 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
